status: analysis proposals only; not current normative requirements/cases

clauses.text: For a MIDI output with Sync enabled, the port-name triangle exposes additional options. Hardware Resync selects a resync behavior when Resync External Hardware is enabled. When enabled, its Control Bar button can send resync messages to external gear. The retained source gives drift during playback as a use context, not an exclusive eligibility gate or successful timing-correction guarantee.

The manual describes Stop and Start as default and as a MIDI Clock Stop event followed by a MIDI Clock Start event; Start Only sends just a Start event; Don’t Resync sends no resync messages. These are symbolic publication claims without byte encoding, timestamps, phase/drift correction, universal device support, constructor/reset observation or exact12.4.3 result.

cases.action: In separately owned future histories admit exact-build feature availability, a usable Sync output and a known compatible external Clock receiver with independently genuine baseline synchronization. Keep input direction/Remote mapping separate. Explicitly enable output Sync, expand the port-name triangle and inspect Hardware Resync. Explicitly enable Resync External Hardware and inspect its Control Bar button. Record actual offered options and control state; a missing port/capability or failed baseline is U, not exclusion proof. Exact option location beyond named Settings/port context and enable-off presentation remain unknown.

First independently establish usable outgoing MIDI Clock from Live and genuine synchronization at a known compatible receiver, with nonzero identifiable active output at Live and receiver; capture baseline traffic and outputs separately. Admit an independently established drifting receiver while Live playback continues for the source use context, without inventing a drift amount or forcing unsafe hardware changes. In three separately reset owned histories explicitly choose Stop and Start, Start Only and Don’t Resync, keep port/source/tempo/transport context declared, then invoke the actually offered Resync External Hardware button. Retain command/control, traffic and receiver observations. Don’t Resync requires a prior genuine positive resync-capable baseline; silence, absent gear, muted output or failed baseline cannot prove suppression. No numeric timing/phase correction or success oracle follows. Drift is a useful documented context, not a claim that command is unavailable without drift.

Future separate proposals must explicitly declare output Sync disabled, feature disabled, port loss/reconnect, receiver incompatibility, multiple outputs, transport stopped/started, preroll/count-in, tempo changes, Song/Pattern setting, repeated invocation, cancellation/undo, save/reopen, rate changes and teardown. Admit independently valid available/working baseline before each negative transition. None of those outcomes is supplied by the selected Resync paragraphs; no destructive resource or hardware trial is authorized.
